narrativeReportMd:
# Narrative R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
No hard instance-breaking changes were found in the local `Narrative` datatype definition. R4 instances that satisfy the required `status` code and valid `div` XHTML constraints should remain representable against the R6 local Narrative shape.

## Scope
The analysis compared the R4 and R6 core StructureDefinitions for `Narrative`, the directly bound `narrative-status` ValueSet and CodeSystem, package indexes, package metadata, and the `xhtml` datatype used by `Narrative.div`. Inherited Element/DataType class hierarchy changes were excluded as required.

## Main migration themes
The local element model is stable: `Narrative.status` remains mandatory `code`, `Narrative.div` remains mandatory `xhtml`, and no local elements were added, removed, renamed, or moved. The only local tooling concern is that R6 consolidates the R4 `txt-1` and `txt-2` `Narrative.div` invariants into a single `txt-1` invariant while preserving the same `htmlChecks()` FHIRPath expression.

## Highest-impact findings
There are no Critical or High findings. The single local finding is a Low runtime/code-generation risk for validators or generated metadata that key on the old `txt-2` invariant id or on the old XPath translations.

## Findings requiring human review
No finding requires human review for basic migration. Reviewers may still want the rendered R6 narrative specification page or official change note if they need to prove the exact intended semantics of `htmlChecks()`.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The invariant consolidation was probably a cleanup rather than a model change. A more backward-compatible design could have retained `txt-2` as a deprecated/alias invariant or retained XPath translations, but that would also preserve duplicate metadata.

## Follow-up analysis
The R6 baseDefinition shift from `Element` to `DataType` should be considered in the DataType/base-infrastructure report. It is intentionally not counted as a local Narrative finding here.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: No hard local R4-to-R6 breaking change was found for `Narrative`. The local data shape, cardinalities, types, required status binding strength, and narrative-status code set are stable. The only notable local risk is a Low tooling/runtime risk from consolidation of `Narrative.div` invariant metadata.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should mostly be transparent for instance content. Systems should continue to populate `Narrative.status` with one of `generated`, `extensions`, `additional`, or `empty`, and `Narrative.div` with the allowed XHTML fragment containing meaningful content. Validator wrappers, test baselines, generated invariant enums, or diagnostics that expect an R4 `txt-2` invariant should be updated to the R6 `txt-1` consolidated invariant.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is High for the local StructureDefinition comparison because both assigned files were present and directly compared, and the complete local CodeSystem concepts for the required binding are unchanged. Confidence is lower only for the external implementation semantics of `htmlChecks()` and for official rationale, which are not fully represented in the StructureDefinition JSON.

findings.title: Narrative.div txt-1 and txt-2 invariants are consolidated under txt-1 in R6

oldState.summary: R4 defined two local error constraints on Narrative.div: txt-1 for the permitted XHTML subset and txt-2 for non-whitespace narrative content. Both constraints used the FHIRPath expression htmlChecks(), and both carried XPath translations.

constraints.human: The narrative SHALL contain only the basic html formatting elements and attributes described in chapters 7-11 (except section 4 of chapter 9) and 15 of the HTML 4.0 standard, <a> elements (either name or href), images and internally contained style attributes
The narrative SHALL have some non-whitespace content

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, tooling could see two separate local invariant identifiers for `Narrative.div`: `txt-1` and `txt-2`.

newState.summary: R6 defines one local error constraint on Narrative.div: txt-1. Its human text combines the permitted XHTML subset rule and the non-whitespace-content rule, still using htmlChecks(). No XPath translation is present.

constraints.human: The narrative SHALL contain only the basic html formatting elements and attributes described in chapters 7-11 (except section 4 of chapter 9) and 15 of the HTML 4.0 standard, <a> elements (either name or href), images and internally contained style attributes, and SHALL contain some non-whitespace characters

newState.narrativeMd: In R6, the same local `Narrative.div` rule surface is represented as a single `txt-1` invariant whose prose includes both the XHTML whitelist and non-whitespace requirements.

facts.note: The separate R4 `txt-2` invariant identifier is not present in R6.
The computable FHIRPath expression used by the local Narrative.div invariant remains the same.

facts.oldValue: Allowed limited XHTML content and attributes.
facts.newValue: Allowed limited XHTML content and attributes, and SHALL contain some non-whitespace characters.
facts.note: The R6 human text folds the R4 txt-2 prose into txt-1.

facts.oldValue: XPath translations supplied for R4 txt-1 and txt-2.
facts.newValue: No XPath translations supplied on the R6 Narrative.div constraints.
facts.note: FHIRPath-based validation is not changed by the missing XPath metadata, but XPath-only tooling may be affected.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `Narrative.div` has the same element id, path, cardinality, type, short text, definition, and comment in both releases. The invariant text and keys show that R6 consolidated R4 `txt-1` and `txt-2` rather than changing the element identity.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not a hard instance-validity break because the local computable FHIRPath expression remains `htmlChecks()` and the R6 prose preserves the same two requirements. The practical risk is for non-instance artifacts: generated invariant constants, validator message baselines, QA tests, XPath-only validation layers, or reporting code that expects a separate `txt-2` diagnostic.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The change affects metadata representation and diagnostics rather than clinical content accepted in `Narrative.div`.

justification.inferredGoal: Reduce duplicate invariant metadata by representing the XHTML whitelist and non-whitespace checks through the single htmlChecks() constraint.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 `txt-2` constraint, and possibly its XPath translation, as deprecated or alias metadata while making the combined R6 `txt-1` rule canonical.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal appears to be metadata cleanup: both R4 `Narrative.div` constraints already used the same `htmlChecks()` expression, and R6 retains the XHTML-subset and non-whitespace requirements in one `txt-1` invariant. That goal is reasonable, and the breakage is limited to generated metadata, invariant IDs, XPath-only tooling, or diagnostic expectations rather than R4 instance content. Given that low impact and the duplication tradeoff, the breaking cleanup was probably proportionate rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would have retained `txt-2` as a deprecated or alias constraint, and possibly retained the R4 XPath translations, while identifying `txt-1` as the canonical consolidated invariant. That would preserve most R4 metadata consumers that key on `txt-2`, but it would also publish two base constraint records for the same `htmlChecks()` validation fact, creating ambiguity about which diagnostic to emit and increasing the chance that obsolete invariant IDs or XPath metadata remain indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves invariant-ID and XPath compatibility, but keeps duplicate same-element constraint metadata and may perpetuate divergent diagnostics for one `htmlChecks()` rule.

evidence.detail: R4 differential lists local Narrative.div constraints `txt-1` and `txt-2`, both with severity `error` and expression `htmlChecks()`.
R6 differential lists only local Narrative.div constraint `txt-1`, with severity `error`, expression `htmlChecks()`, and combined human text including the non-whitespace requirement.
evidence.quote: txt-1; expression htmlChecks(); and SHALL contain some non-whitespace characters

evidence.detail: R4 supplies XPath translations for the `txt-1` and `txt-2` constraints.
R6 does not include XPath translations on the Narrative.div constraint records.

examples.examplesMd: No instance JSON example is included because this finding is about invariant metadata identity and validator diagnostics, not about a changed JSON/XML instance shape or an old-valid/new-invalid content pattern.

findings.narrativeMd: `Narrative.div` remains required XHTML, but the invariant metadata changed. R4 exposed two local constraints, `txt-1` and `txt-2`; R6 exposes one `txt-1` whose prose covers both the allowed-XHTML rule and the non-whitespace-content rule. Implementers who only validate instance content through FHIRPath should not see a new invalid/valid boundary from this StructureDefinition change. Implementers who generate code, constants, documentation, or QA expectations from invariant keys may need to remove references to `txt-2` or map them to R6 `txt-1`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `Narrative.div` does not become invalid solely because `txt-2` disappeared: the R6 constraint still calls `htmlChecks()` and its human text still requires non-whitespace content. Valid R6 `Narrative.div` content is also not blocked from R4 representation by this metadata change. The compatibility issue is runtime/tooling oriented: strict consumers of StructureDefinition constraint arrays, XPath-only validators, and tests that assert specific invariant IDs or messages can observe a break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update generated invariant catalogs and validator baselines so R6 `Narrative.div` diagnostics are keyed to `txt-1` only. If a migration layer reports historical R4 validation results, map R4 `txt-2` to the R6 `txt-1` narrative-content check for user-facing explanations. Test both invalid XHTML markup and whitespace-only narratives to ensure the R6 validator still enforces both halves of `htmlChecks()`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This change was probably avoidable from a metadata-compatibility perspective: the specification could have retained `txt-2` as a deprecated alias invariant or continued emitting XPath translations. That would have been gentler for tools but would also preserve redundant constraints around the same `htmlChecks()` function. Because no instance content is lost and the duplicated R4 expression already pointed at the same helper, the cleanup appears proportionate.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: If a downstream validator's `htmlChecks()` implementation changed outside the StructureDefinition JSON, that would be a separate runtime validation issue. The local JSON evidence does not show such a change.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The affected path remains `Narrative.div` with cardinality `1..1` and type `xhtml`. R4 exposed two error invariants, `txt-1` and `txt-2`, while R6 exposes one `txt-1` invariant whose text combines the XHTML-subset and non-whitespace requirements. The computable FHIRPath expression remains `htmlChecks()`, so this finding does not show an R4-valid narrative becoming invalid in R6 or an R6 narrative becoming unrepresentable in R4. The observable migration issue is for tools that key diagnostics, generated constants, or test baselines on the removed `txt-2` invariant ID, or that depended on the removed XPath translations. That is metadata/tooling churn rather than a meaningful exchange or validation-boundary break for narrative content.
keyEvidence: Reviewed docs/fresh-review-judgment-framework.md; metadata churn without practical compatibility risk can be judged No problem.
R4 StructureDefinition-Narrative.json has Narrative.div min 1 max 1 type xhtml with local error constraints txt-1 and txt-2, both using expression htmlChecks().
R6 StructureDefinition-Narrative.json has Narrative.div min 1 max 1 type xhtml with one local error constraint txt-1 using expression htmlChecks() and combined human text.
R4 snapshot/differential include XPath translations for txt-1 and txt-2; R6 Narrative.div constraints do not include XPath translations.
R4 maturity/status evidence checked: Narrative is normative in the supplied context and local maturity map/StructureDefinition.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 Narrative is normative, which raises the stability expectation for real instance-validity, runtime, or conformance breaks. Here the path shape and computable validation expression are stable, so the normative status does not turn the removed duplicate invariant ID into a review-worthy compatibility concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: the strongest mechanism is changed StructureDefinition constraint metadata, especially removal of the separate txt-2 key and XPath translations; no old-valid/new-invalid instance break is evident.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking base design could have retained txt-2 as a legacy/alias constraint and kept the old XPath translations. That would help invariant-ID or XPath-driven tools, but it would also publish duplicate constraint records for the same htmlChecks() validation fact, create diagnostic precedence ambiguity, and preserve obsolete metadata. The tradeoff is not compelling when instance semantics are unchanged.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low-impact/no-hard-instance-break assessment and its view that only a partial less-breaking alternative exists; under the fresh framework this is best treated as metadata/tooling churn with no meaningful compatibility problem.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, active status, abstract=false flag, and normative status are preserved. The baseDefinition shift to `DataType` is explicitly excluded as a base-artifact/class-hierarchy issue.
The local differential still contains `Narrative`, `Narrative.status`, and `Narrative.div`. No local element was added, removed, renamed, split, or moved.
`Narrative.status` remains `1..1`, `Narrative.div` remains `1..1`, and the root snapshot remains `0..*`. Inherited `id` and `extension` cardinalities are not local findings.

`Narrative.status` remains type `code`; `Narrative.div` remains type `xhtml`. The inspected R4/R6 `xhtml` StructureDefinitions keep the same primitive type identity and value cardinality for the relevant XHTML value.

`Narrative.status` remains required-bound to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/narrative-status`; the bound version changes from `4.0.1` to `6.0.0-ballot4`, but the local complete CodeSystem concepts are unchanged.

The only local constraint delta is the `Narrative.div` invariant consolidation captured in finding `Narrative:SERIALIZATION_OR_CODEGEN:Narrative.div:txt-merge`. No material accepted-content change is evident from the StructureDefinition because the computable expression remains `htmlChecks()`.
No fixed value, pattern value, or default value is present on local Narrative elements in either release.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex value-limit delta was found.
`Narrative`, `Narrative.status`, and `Narrative.div` remain `isModifier=false` in the compared snapshots.
`Narrative.status` and `Narrative.div` remain `isSummary=false`; the root summary flag remains absent/null.
No slicing is present on local Narrative elements in either release.

The local short, definition, and comment text for `Narrative`, `Narrative.status`, and `Narrative.div` are materially stable. The constraint prose consolidation is handled separately as a tooling-risk finding.
No JSON/XML instance representation change was found for local Narrative content. The limitation is metadata-level: invariant keys and XPath translations changed for `Narrative.div`.
R6 local Narrative instances using the same `status` codes and XHTML `div` content are representable in R4. No R6-only local element, type, or code was identified.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Narrative.status binding now references the R6 ballot version of narrative-status
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Narrative.status` remains a required `code` bound to the same canonical ValueSet URL, and the complete CodeSystem concepts remain `generated`, `extensions`, `additional`, and `empty` with the same displays and definitions. Instances carry only the code value, so no R4-valid status code becomes invalid based on the local terminology files.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology loaders and validators should use the R6 `6.0.0-ballot4` package version when validating R6 artifacts, but no ConceptMap or code transform is needed for the local code set.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Root metadata refreshed while canonical identity and normative status remain stable
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 updates package/build metadata such as publisher, contact, jurisdiction, generated narrative text on terminology resources, and working group extension. These do not alter the canonical datatype identity or instance validation shape.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Tools that display artifact metadata may show updated publisher/contact/jurisdiction values. This should not require data migration.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Narrative.baseDefinition` is `DataType` rather than R4 `Element`. Per the inherited/base-artifact scope rule, any class hierarchy, inherited field, or generated superclass implications should be assessed in the DataType/base-infrastructure report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff or change note was available locally, so the rationale for consolidating `txt-1`/`txt-2` is inferred from the StructureDefinition deltas.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official HL7 change note or rendered diff for `Narrative` would confirm whether the invariant change was intended as a metadata cleanup.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The StructureDefinitions reference `htmlChecks()` but do not define the full runtime implementation of that helper. This report can compare the constraint expression and prose, but cannot prove that every R4 and R6 validator implements `htmlChecks()` identically.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Comparing the rendered narrative specification pages and validator source/version notes for `htmlChecks()` would resolve whether there are runtime validation changes outside the StructureDefinition.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No terminology server expansion was executed. The confidence impact is low because the ValueSet compose includes all codes from a complete local CodeSystem, and the CodeSystem concepts are unchanged between the inspected R4 and R6 packages.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Running expansions for both ValueSet versions with the same terminology server would independently confirm the unchanged code set.
